reviews.reason: The corner-order proof uses only e>=2: a same-row or adjacent same-column mixed pair has content difference 1 and cannot share a residue. Transposition preserves corner type, reverses content order and negates residues; identical sign words have identical stack-reduction survivors. None of these steps identifies general e with a prime characteristic. Item unchanged; refreshed the obsolete supplier Definition quotations for F2 and F4 in the batch-16 contract only.

Parts 1 and 2 transport the regular QG empty component and its decomposition by conjugation and diagram reflection for every finite e>=2. Part 3 separately assumes e=p and xi=1; sign tensoring negates each JM element, giving the stated residue-negated socle formula. Part 4 uses integer contents and finite good deletions at e=0. The declared AC use remains confined to the decomposition supplier. Item unchanged; refreshed obsolete supplier quotations for F1 and F7 in the batch-16 contract only.

At e=3, (4) is nonrestricted and its conjugate (1,1,1,1) is nonregular. The AC-bearing top-isotypic lattice splitting injects the basic residue space into the ambient chart, so independence excludes both the standard vector and its congruent ambient global lift. The residue-0 deletion (4)->(3) stays outside the empty component. These checks use the revised finite-e convention without an unqualified characteristic identification. Item unchanged; refreshed the F1 supplier quotation in the batch-16 contract only.

Its Fock clause uses general e-restricted labels and all-partition standard vectors. The ordinary/Murphy dictionary retains the theta pullback, inverse JM eigenvalues and reflected content instead of an untwisted same-block identification. No use requires general e to be prime.
